releases.name: Anka 1.0.1
releases.body:
**Anka 1.0.1** opens games stored as **.nup** packages.

Built from [`anka`](https://github.com/EddizEge/Anka/tree/anka) at `2d17a71ff0f0cf0c27b3d7207818fade9199b77b`; both programs carry this commit.

## Updating from 1.0.0

Close Anka, unzip **`Anka-1.0.1-win64.zip`** into your Anka folder and replace the files. Your `user` folder (settings, keys, firmware and saves) stays as it is.

New to Anka: follow the quick start in the [1.0.0 notes](https://github.com/EddizEge/Anka/releases/tag/anka-v1.0.0). Unzip into a new, empty folder, start `anka.exe`, and install your own keys and firmware.

## What's in 1.0.1

### .nup packages
- `.nup` ("Unencrypted (Archival) Package") is a container format from upstream Eglantine. It holds one title's base game, update and add-on content in a single file.
- Anka now **reads** .nup files. You can open them with **File › Load File…**, and they appear in the game list with their icon, name and version. `anka-cli.exe` and its launchers open them too, including from the `Games` folder.
- Mods (LayeredFS) and Anka's game-specific settings apply to games opened from a .nup, the same as for other formats. Anka finds the title ID before the game starts.

releases.name: Anka 1.0.0
releases.body:
First release of **Anka**, a Nintendo Switch 2 emulator for Windows, focused on performance.

Built from [`anka`](https://github.com/EddizEge/Anka/tree/anka) at `b7542ece8b5c695e2f01d5e46b74c0806d48ae96`; both programs carry this commit.

## Quick start

1. Unzip **`Anka-1.0.0-win64.zip`** into a **new, empty folder**. Do not unzip it into another emulator's folder: its Qt DLLs would replace that program's.
2. Start **`anka.exe`**. Anka keeps its settings, keys, firmware and saves in the `user` folder next to it (portable mode) and does not touch `%APPDATA%\eden` or other installs.
3. Install your own keys and firmware as with other Eden-based emulators. Anka includes no games, keys or firmware; only use what you legally own.
4. Settings: **Emulation › Configure… › Anka**. The first start picks *Recommended*, the setup we measured (with GPU Mode *Fast*, the default; it also turns Reactive Flushing off).

Coming from PokeDinner-Eglantine 2.0.0: back up its `nand` folder (your saves), then copy its `user` folder next to `anka.exe`.

Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) and a GPU with a current Vulkan driver. Qt and the Visual C++ runtime come with Anka.

## What's in 1.0.0

from different nights stay distinguishable after you have downloaded them.

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.9.5
releases.body: # ARMSX2 2.9.5 What's new: ## Memory cards **Folder memory cards keep every save.** If your memory card's Type is Folder, every save is now written whole. A save made just before you left the app could come back blank or as the older version, because the card was written to storage between the save's data and its file entry; that can no longer happen. A new save that reuses a deleted save's space keeps its own name instead of reappearing under the deleted one's. A save file the device won't open for writing is still read, where the game showed it as damaged. New saves are created on storage that needs Android's own file access with the IOP thread on, and leaving the app rewrites nothing when nothing on the card changed. done by @bmdhacks

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.9.4
releases.body: # ARMSX2 2.9.4 ## New **Vulkan by default.** New installs start on the Vulkan renderer on every device whose driver reports Vulkan 1.1, and on Auto elsewhere. Existing installs keep the renderer they have. Auto now picks Vulkan on every Mali of the Bifrost G31, G51, G52 and G76 generation and of the Valhall generations (G57 to G78, G310 to G710, G615, G715, Immortalis-G715). done by @bmdhacks **MaliSX2 on every Mali it drives.** The GPU Driver list, the GPU card, first-run setup and the driver notice offer MaliSX2 on the Mali-G31, G51, G52 and G76, G57, G68, G77 and G78, G310, G510, G610 and G710, and G615, G715 and Immortalis-G715. The G31, G51 and G310 to G710 need MaliSX2 0.5.0 or newer. done by @bmdhacks

New audio, rendering, and Android startup fixes are here. Huge thanks to

work, and [AlanConstantino](https://github.com/AlanConstantino) for integrating
it and testing on Retroid Pocket 6 in [PR #123](https://github.com/Buku313/Skate3-Mobile/pull/123).
Alex McHugh's Skate3Recomp and ReXGlue/Xenia remain the foundation of this port.

## Download

Most players want **Skate3-Mobile-Android.apk**. Install over your existing
main app. Do not uninstall first. Android will ask you to approve the update.
Your extracted game files stay in place.

[Download the main APK](https://github.com/Buku313/Skate3-Mobile/releases/download/v2.1.0/Skate3-Mobile-Android.apk)
or [get the separate QA Build](https://github.com/Buku313/Skate3-Mobile/releases/download/v2.1.0-qa1/Skate3-Mobile-QA.apk).
The debug APK is for users of the separate developer app.

Older QA and developer builds used the main app's update address. Install the
matching v2.1 APK once, without uninstalling. From this version onward, each
app receives updates for its own package only.

# Skate 3 Mobile v2.0.18 QA 6

This QA build targets an intermittent early-boot hang reported on the Retroid Pocket 5.

The failed QA 5 diagnostic showed a live audio thread but no first presentation, native pipeline creation, scene target, or crash. The guest render thread stopped immediately after its first offscreen 2D captures.

QA 6 tightens the boot capture boundary:

- Only the four verified 2D vertex layouts and three supported primitive types are accepted.
- Individual and per-frame 2D payloads have conservative size limits.
- Invalid transient draw state is rejected before reading guest memory.
- The first twelve guest frames now log capture begin and completion markers.

releases.body:
# Skate 3 Mobile v2.0.18 QA 5

This is an opt-in diagnostic build that installs over earlier **Skate 3 QA** builds and preserves QA app data.

## RP5 intermittent black-screen fix

QA 4 proved that the Retroid Pocket 5 can render the Quality profile's 1280x720 scene target, but testers reported that startup only succeeded roughly half the time.

The QA 4 profile copied Performance's visible feature settings, but one internal pipeline gate still used the profile number. Quality therefore compiled optional outline, spline, and shadow shader families even though those features were disabled. Cold and partially warmed shader caches could take different startup paths.

QA 5 fixes the mismatch:

- The 1280x720 Quality target remains enabled.
- The pipeline builder now follows the active lean-scene flag instead of assuming every Quality profile needs the full optional PSO set.
- Renderer installation applies the same defensive lean-feature guard.
- The startup log must report `lean Android set` for this QA Quality profile.
- Stable v2.0.17 and its update channel remain unchanged.

## RP5 test

1. Install QA 5 directly over QA 4.
2. Keep the System Driver selected.

**Game Format Converter 2.1.0** (formerly CHD Manager) adds a lot of formats. Everything new is described honestly in the README, including what was and wasn't tested.

## What's new

- **A new name.** CHD Manager is now Game Format Converter, because it converts far more than CHDs. It lives at a new repository address with new file names. **If you have an older CHD Manager, download this release once by hand: the old program can't find it by itself.** Your settings and keys don't carry over; put them in again under Settings for the optional features that use them.
- **Xbox 360:** ZAR (for Xenia), ISO and game folders. Hex-named download packages (Xbox Live Arcade, Games on Demand) aren't discs, so they are refused with an explanation.
- **Original Xbox:** a full dump becomes a trimmed `.xiso.iso` (7.8 GB down to just the game); also game folders and CHD.
- **PlayStation 3:** game folder to ISO and back, split pieces joined, `.pkg` packages unpacked and packed (with your own RPCS3 or your own key).
- **Nintendo Switch:** NSP to XCI and back, bundles with the newest update and DLC, one NSP per title, swapping in a newer update. **Switch 2:** folder to NUP and back (experimental).

## What's new

- **New formats.** CSO and ZSO (PSP/PS2), ECM, and the GameCube/Wii family: ISO, RVZ, WIA, WBFS, GCZ and CISO, plus Wii U WUX/WUD in both directions. Archives (zip, tar, gz, 7z, rar) can be added directly.

releases.name: WWE '12 PC 1.5.0 "Small PCs"
releases.body:
# WWE '12 PC 1.5.0 "Small PCs"

This version is about PCs with few or slow CPU cores: a start-up freeze is fixed, parts of the game run faster, and there is a new FPS counter. It also fixes two Universe problems.

## Fixes

- **Fixed a rare freeze on "NOW LOADING" at start-up** on PCs with few or slow CPU cores (a race between the game's sound-bank loading threads). The game could stay on the first loading screen forever. On a test PC limited to 2 slow cores it froze in 2 starts out of 10 before the fix and never in 10 starts after it (#69, #74: if your freeze has another cause, tell us). 
- **No more loading-screen speed-up on PCs with fewer than 8 usable threads**, where it could lock the game at its frame barrier.
- **Universe: SmackDown (and other weekly shows) no longer end up with only 0-1 match** when their roster is small: a match that would be dropped because everyone is resting now takes a rested Superstar instead.

releases.name: WWE '12 PC 1.4.1
releases.body:
# WWE '12 PC 1.4.1

A small update after 1.4.0: a Royal Rumble crash fixed, and belt modding in the Mod Maker.

## Fixes

- **Royal Rumble crash (#79):** in 1.4.0, the animations added for the I QUIT match were loaded in **every** match. The Royal Rumble, which loads the most wrestlers, could run out of room in the game's animation memory and crash, or leave wrestlers frozen and entrants stuck behind the ramp. They are now only added in an **I QUIT** match or a **Special Guest Referee** match; every other match is the original game again. I QUIT and the special referee work as before.

## Mod Maker

- **Belt modding.** In BELTS & WEAPONS, a new **Port a belt from another game** page: bring a title belt from WWE 2K14, 2K15, WWE '13, 2K16 / 2K17 or SvR 2007-2011 in place of one of the game's belts, with its menu pictures (belt, background, statistics, unlock icons). It is a new `belt` mod type, handled by the game and the launcher. Seen in game with the 2K14 WWE title at the waist; the other games, hand and shoulder poses are less tested. You cannot add a 24th title (the save has 23): replace one you do not use.
- Updated HELP page.

## Android

releases.name: v1.4.0
releases.body:
# WWE '12 PC 1.4.0

The match-options update: new match rules in the menus (starting finishers, squash, I QUIT, Special Guest Referee), a Universe chaos level, Mod Maker additions and fixes for what you reported after 1.3.0.

## New match options

- **Starting finishers (as in WWE 2K14).** On the character select, press **LT / RT** on a place to choose how many finishers that wrestler starts with: NONE, 1, 2, 3 or INFINITE. It shows in the title of the attire frame (or in the READY banner for wrestlers with only one attire). Left on NORMAL, nothing changes. *Limit:* in a few match types the game skips the attire frame, so the option is only offered in a normal 1 on 1.
- **Squash matches.** In **OPTIONS > GAMEPLAY > BALANCING > DAMAGE** (the page now has three new lines): **SQUASH CHANCE** (0-100 %, the chance that a 1 on 1 match is a squash; 0 = off, the default), **SQUASH: JOBBER HEALTH** (starting health of the lower-rated wrestler, 20 % by default) and **STARTING FINISHERS** (default for every match). The lower-rated wrestler is the jobber; the other one starts with a finisher. The labels of the three new lines are in English only.

releases.name: v1.3.0
releases.body:
**WWE '12 PC v1.3.0 — "Speed and fixes"**

> ⚠️ No game data included: you need your own copy of WWE '12 for Xbox 360.

### Faster
- **Loading screens shorter** (a match loads in about 1.5 s instead of 4 s, the end of the entrances in about 1.9 s instead of 4.5 s). `wwe12_fast_loading = false` brings the old behaviour back.
- **Faster start-up** on PCs with 8 or more logical processors: the title screen comes after about 5-7 s instead of 15 s. On smaller processors the normal start-up is kept (`wwe12_fast_boot_min_threads`).
- **Sharper picture** when the game is drawn at 720p on a bigger screen (`svr_upscale_sharpness`, 0 turns it off).
- **Adaptive V-sync**: a late frame is shown at once instead of waiting a whole refresh (`svr_adaptive_vsync`).
- **Performance test** in the launcher (button *Performance test*): it plays a recorded 1-on-1 match with entrances once and tells you if your PC is fine, limited by the processor or by the graphics card. Nothing is changed without your agreement.

### Frame rate

**WWE '12 PC v1.2.0 — "Moveset update"**

> ⚠️ No game data included: you need your own copy of WWE '12 for Xbox 360.

### Fixed
- **Match-start stutter (and a short freeze) on integrated graphics (Intel...)**: the game's reads of the picture back from the graphics card are now grouped at the end of the frame (about 10 times less waiting at the start of a match). `svr_readback_defer_streak = false` goes back to 1.1.
- **Less work for the processor every frame** (helps small PCs, issue #53): shader constants are reused like on Android (`svr_reuse_constant_blocks`) and the check of 3D models is lighter (`svr_geometry_sample_min`, 32768 brings the 1.1 behaviour back).
- **Crash at start with file names that have accents or other characters** (for example a song called "Café.mp3" or a mod folder with Japanese letters in a mod): names are now read as UTF-8 everywhere in the game, the launcher and the Mod Maker, and a mod with an unreadable name is skipped instead of closing the game.
- **Launcher: the MUSIC page closed the launcher** when a file in the `music` folder had an odd name.

**What's new**

- Intel Macs are supported. There are now two Mac downloads, one for Apple Silicon (M1 and later) and one for Intel Macs.

- Game details are built in. Information on over 4,000 DOS games now ships with TurboStage, so game details appear instantly, even offline. Cover art and screenshots still download when needed.

- New About window with the version and credits (in the Help menu, or the TurboStage menu on Mac).

**Fixes**

- Some older CD-ROM images could not be scanned (for example Power Drive). They are now recognized.
- Some games did not start when their archive contained several copies of the start file (for example Power Drive).
- The MT-32 / Sound Canvas choice in a game's Setup tab is now always applied.
- New File > Show DOSBox log, to see what happened when a game doesn't start or has no sound.

**Upgrading**

releases.name: BOTWRecompAndroid 0.4.11 (beta 43): o jogo não fecha mais por falta de memória no Adreno 640
releases.body:
**Beta 43.** Uma correção para o jogo que fechava depois de alguns minutos num Adreno 6xx com 8 GB de RAM.

## Adreno 6xx com 8 GB de RAM (#520)

O log do OnePlus 7 Pro (Adreno 640, 8 GB) mostrou que a GPU ficava sem memória: depois de 8 a 28 minutos, o driver não conseguia mais criar os pipelines (os "programas" que desenham cada tipo de objeto), e o jogo fechava logo depois.

- **A causa:** no Turnip, a opção **Memória do jogo na GPU (Turnip)** no Automático coloca os ~3,1 GB da memória do jogo direto na GPU. Num aparelho com 8 GB, isso deixava pouca memória para o próprio driver.
- **O que muda:** num Adreno 6xx com 8 GB de RAM ou menos, o Automático agora deixa essa opção desligada, e o jogo trabalha com cópias. A tela inicial avisa isso embaixo da opção. Com cópias, o mesmo aparelho jogou 2 horas sem fechar, com o texto certo e de 13 a 16 fps (antes, de 10 a 14). Quem quiser pode ligar a opção na mão.
- **E se a memória acabar mesmo assim:** antes, um pipeline que falhava por falta de memória ficava perdido até o fim da sessão, e o que ele desenhava sumia. Agora os pipelines sem uso são liberados na hora, e o que falhou é criado de novo 5 s depois.

releases.name: BOTWRecompAndroid 0.4.10 (beta 42): uma correção para o travamento na Mali
releases.body:
**Beta 42.** Uma correção para o travamento depois de alguns minutos nas GPUs que trabalham no modo cópia (Mali e o driver de fábrica da Qualcomm).

## O travamento depois de alguns minutos (#401, #489)

Os logs da 0.4.9 mostraram que o problema não era a ordem das threads nos núcleos: com a opção nova ligada, o jogo travou do mesmo jeito, e o laço estava no **alocador de memória do jogo**, que percorria uma lista de blocos livres danificada.

- **A causa provável:** nessas GPUs, o que um shader grava na memória do jogo volta para ela depois que a GPU termina. Cada pedaço era conferido ("a GPU mudou, o jogo não") e depois copiado inteiro. Se uma thread do jogo escrevesse no mesmo pedaço entre as duas coisas, por exemplo nos dados que o alocador guarda ao lado de cada bloco, essa escrita se perdia. Uma escrita perdida ali deixa a lista de blocos livres em laço, e o jogo para.
- **A correção:** só volta o que a GPU mudou, palavra por palavra, e cada palavra só é escrita se o jogo não a mudou nesse meio-tempo. A escrita do jogo nunca se perde.

releases.name: BOTWRecompAndroid 0.4.9 (beta 41): uma opção contra o travamento, e telas mais quadradas
releases.body:
**Beta 41.** Uma opção experimental para o travamento depois de alguns minutos, um relatório de travamento mais completo, o modo Livre em telas mais quadradas que 16:9, e menos cópias de constantes na Mali.

## O travamento depois de alguns minutos (#401)

Os logs da 0.4.8 mostraram onde ele para: a thread principal do jogo fica presa para sempre percorrendo uma lista dos efeitos do jogo que foi danificada antes. O código de efeitos do jogo escolhe uma área de trabalho pelo número do núcleo da CPU em que a thread está. No Switch, duas threads do mesmo núcleo nunca rodam ao mesmo tempo; aqui isso só valia para o núcleo 0, então duas threads dos núcleos 1 ou 2 podiam usar a mesma área de uma vez.

- **Nova opção: Configurações > Turnos por núcleo como no Switch (experimental).** As threads que dividem um núcleo se revezam nos núcleos 0 a 2, e não só no 0. Vem desligada. Quem tem o travamento: ligue, jogue como antes e conte se ainda trava. Vale na próxima vez que o jogo iniciar.
- **Relatório de travamento:** as threads que estão rodando dizem em que função do app estão e de qual núcleo seguram a vez, e as que ficam paradas numa função do app ou segurando a vez mostram onde estão.

releases.name: BOTWRecompAndroid 0.4.8 (beta 40): caçando o travamento, e texturas sem esperas
releases.body:
**Beta 40.** Correções para threads do jogo que podiam ficar esperando para sempre, um relatório de travamento que mostra onde a thread principal do jogo está, e trocas de textura sem esperar a thread de render em toda GPU.

## O travamento depois de alguns minutos (#401, #489)

Os primeiros logs da 0.4.7 mostraram que **não é a GPU**: quando trava, a thread principal do jogo segura o "núcleo 0" (o app faz as threads desse núcleo se revezarem, como no Switch) e não larga, enquanto as outras esperam. Uma delas pediu para dormir 100 ms e ficou 10 s esperando atrás dela.

- **Relatório de travamento:** além da lista de threads, o log agora diz quem segura o núcleo 0, há quanto tempo, quem está na fila, e onde a thread que o segura está naquele momento. Quem tem o travamento: espere uns 15 s depois de travar, feche o app e mande o `botwrecomp-log-previous.txt` (Configurações > Arquivos).

releases.name: BOTWRecompAndroid 0.4.7 (beta 39): mapa certo com a Economia de RAM, opção de sombras e menos esperas por shaders
releases.body:
**Beta 39.** O mapa e o minimapa não ficam mais escuros com a Economia de RAM ligada, chega a opção Vídeo > Sombras, e o jogo espera menos por shaders. Várias mudanças vieram de colaboradores (obrigado, Propinbo e HallanBR!).

## Correções

- **Mapa e minimapa escuros com a "Economia de RAM" ligada (#471, #478):** com o zoom no mapa, ou no minimapa, a imagem ficava escura.
  - **Causa:** com a Economia de RAM, depois de enviar uma textura à GPU o app devolvia a memória dela ao Android, e essa memória passava a ler zeros. Mas o jogo às vezes cria a textura de novo sobre a mesma memória sem carregar o arquivo outra vez, e ela era enviada a partir dos zeros.
  - **Agora:** a memória vai para o swap do Android com o conteúdo guardado: a economia continua, e nada vira zero. Se você tinha o problema, conte se resolveu.
- **Frame rate 40 / 45 em telas de 120 Hz (#455):** o HyperOS deixa o jogo em 60 Hz até ele pedir mais, e o modo caía para 30. Agora o app pergunta ao Android a maior taxa que a tela oferece e pede 120 Hz. Contribuição do HallanBR.

releases.name: melonRA 0.5.1
releases.body:
# Changes (**Mainly bugfixes!**)
- Linux: Accepting a Netplay invite through Discord without having melonRA open would show an "Unknown protocol" error message, this was because it wasn't registered properly with the rest of apps in the OS, it now handles it properly.
- Netplay: Errors whilst syncing up instances and saves with the "hidden consoles" used for Netplay.
- Netplay: Closing the room closes the open UDP port after a while.
- Netplay: Closing a room with nobody connected is now instant.
- _Other minor Netplay fixes._
- Rewind kept its history after inserting a cartridge or booting up firmware. Meaning that, rewinding could make you rewind to a previous game. This has been patched.
- _Other general fixes._
- Casual mode offline unlocks were dropped if the saved login expired when its sent, now it is kept for the next login. And now the text is clearer when you play offline.

releases.name: melonRA 0.5.0
releases.body:
# Additions and changes
- There's a new and more concise **settings window** which shows all categories of settings in the same window without having to close and open them separately.
- **The name of the game is shown in the window title now, as well as its icon in the taskbar.**
- **"Hybrid Single"** as a new screen layout mode, literally the same as _Hybrid_, but without the mirroring of the top screen. _(Perfect for dyslexic people, like me! :D)_
- New **Time Played** and **Last Played** columns on the game list.
- **New option to mark games as "Favorite"** (it shows with a little heart besides the title, same place as the mastery and game settings cog) and a new tab for all favorite games.
- The ability to **make a desktop shortcut** for any game, which uses the actual icon of the ROM.
- **Thumbnails** for every save state slot.
- New option to **resume where you left off last session.** (Found in _Interface Settings_)
- New Rewind hotkey, must be enabled also in _Interface Settings_ alongside the amount of seconds you can rewind back to.
- **Trimmed the executable** so its a smaller download overall.

# XRecomp 0.19.1

<!-- Highlights: what changed, what works, known problems. Written by hand, kept across updates. -->

Fixes from the first problem reports sent from the app, plus the performance work since 0.19.0.

- **Long disc image paths** (Android, macOS, Linux): host paths were capped at 260 bytes and cut without a word. An
  ISO with a long name in a deep folder made `<image>/base/textures/saveimage.xbx` the `textures` folder, so files
  under the disc did not open; DOOM 3 lost most of `base/` and showed « dirty disc » after its first save. Paths now
  go up to 4096 bytes, and one that still does not fit fails with a warning instead of naming another file.
- **A Prepare queued behind another title** shows its place in the queue on the Preparing screen. It showed
  « Stopped » with Retry, and its automatic report went out as « PrepareFailed: ? ». Only a failed Prepare is
  reported now.
- **Benchmark** in the game menu: 60 s from the newest save state (or from boot); its result is sent only on Send.
  Game runs can send a performance summary (opt-in, as the crash reports).

releases.name: XRecomp v0.19.0
releases.body:
# XRecomp 0.19.0

<!-- Highlights: what changed, what works, known problems. Written by hand, kept across updates. -->

A second Xbox 360 performance night, measured headless on Warhammer: Battle March. Frames and save states are byte
identical to 0.18.0, except where a change is opt-in or per title (below).

- **Guest CPU**: `MmQueryStatistics` keeps a page count instead of scanning (it was half of the boot's host CPU). The
  VMX helpers work on 16- and 8-bit lanes, use the compiler's vector extensions and are inlined. Host CPU: the boot
  is 3× faster and in-game play 1.8× (141 → 79 ms of guest time per swap). The scheduler turn is cheaper and makes
  the same decisions. Prepare is not slower: the VMX-heavy files compile 27–41 % faster with NDK clang.
- **Renderer**: 16-bit resolve formats take the fast path, and the stencil is read back in 2 passes instead of 8.
  Tiled addressing is worked out per tile row, texture rows are read 16 bytes at a time, texture memory is hashed in
  8 lanes and packed vertex formats use tables. Renderer CPU per swap is about half of 0.18.0's.

releases.name: XRecomp v0.18.0
releases.body:
# XRecomp 0.18.0

<!-- Highlights: what changed, what works, known problems. Written by hand, kept across updates. -->

A speed night on every console but the Xbox 360. Every change is bit-exact: frame, RAM and audio hashes over 600
frames or more are identical to 0.17.0, and lockstep with the interpreters holds.

| Console | x86-64 instructions per frame (bench) | Prepare again? |
|---|---|---|
| GBA | 9.06M → 7.09M (−22 %) | yes |
| PS1 | 8.08M → 6.49M (−20 %) | no |
| N64 | 6.58M → 5.65M (−14 %) | yes |
| GameCube | audio mix −24 %, GX front end −14 % | no |
| Xbox | float stack code −30 % on arm64 (`fistp` without libm) | yes |

releases.body:
Twelfth beta of KINGDOM HEARTS 358/2 Days for Android on **[khdays-port 0.1.5](https://github.com/Yokimitsuro/khdays-port/releases/tag/v0.1.5)**, Yokimitsuro's native PC port that this Android version follows. All the credit for the port itself goes there.

Coming from an earlier beta? The game offers this update itself on the title screen, or install the APK below by hand; your game, HD files and saves are kept.

## What's new since beta 11

A beta about speed with the HD pack's KH2 models.

- **Scenes with the KH2 character models are no longer slow.** A KH2 model with a coat made the whole 3D picture take a slow path. On a Mali-G57 tablet the scene after Day 7 ran at 16-22 pictures a second; now 51-60. Stronger devices gain too in close-ups.
- **Enhanced character shadows cost much less.** With the setting on, an AYN Thor went from 93 to 62 pictures a second in the Grey Area; now 86.
- **A frozen picture on Mali devices is recovered from.** When the graphics driver stopped answering, the picture stood still for good while the game went on. The game now notices and carries on after a short hitch, and one of the two moments where it happened is gone.

A small beta about starting the game.

- **Much faster starts on some devices.** The graphics card's programs are now kept between starts instead of being made again every time. On the AYN Odin (Adreno 630) the screen stayed black for one to four minutes at every start; now it is about 3 seconds. Other devices start a little faster too.

releases.name: v0.1.0
releases.body:
The first release of Odin.

Odin (ᚨ) is a low-level emulator of the SEGA Hikaru arcade board. It runs the programs of the real chips wherever they are known, and draws with OpenGL or Vulkan. It is a hard fork of Valkyrie, by Stefano Teso.

## Games

All six Hikaru games, two of them in two versions:

- Air Trix (`airtrix`, `airtrixo`)
- Brave Firefighters (`braveff`)
- Planet Harriers (`pharrier`)
- NASCAR Arcade (`sgnascar`, `sgnascaro`)
- Star Wars Racer Arcade (`swracer`)
- Cyber Troopers Virtual-On Force (`von4`)

They play with a keyboard, mice, gamepads, wheels with force feedback (NASCAR) or light guns (Brave Firefighters). Each game is a MAME ROM and needs the BIOS `hikaru.zip` and `mie.zip` too.

## Downloads

| File | For |
|---|---|
| odin-v0.1.0-windows-x86_64.zip | Windows 10 or 11 |
| odin-x86_64.AppImage / odin-v0.1.0-linux-x86_64.tar.gz | Linux PC with glibc 2.38 or later (e.g. Ubuntu 24.04) |
| odin-aarch64.AppImage / odin-v0.1.0-linux-aarch64.tar.gz | Linux ARM64 with glibc 2.38 or later and OpenGL ES 3.1 |
| odin-macos.dmg | Mac with Apple silicon, macOS 13.3 or later |
| Odin-Artwork.zip | The title screens and bezels of the games |

TNRP Alpha 2.2.2 — hotfix for Android.

Linux and Windows stay on Alpha 2.2.1: https://github.com/thebabyhippo303/nimbus-recompilation-project/releases/tag/alpha-2.2.1

# Nimbus Alpha 2.2.2 for Android

A second hotfix for Android. Linux and Windows stay on 2.2.1.

## Fixed

- **Phones that still showed "Nimbus could not start graphics" on 2.2.1** (for example some Helio G99 phones on Android 14) now start their games. On these phones Nimbus uses a second graphics path.
- Heads up: the second graphics path is slower than Vulkan, so games on those phones may run slower. Every other device stays on Vulkan.
- Every other device runs exactly as on 2.2.1.

## Good to know

- After updating, Nimbus prepares its shaders once more on the first start.
- Online play is unchanged: 2.2.2 on Android plays with 2.2, 2.2.1 and 2.2.2 on every platform.

## Updating

Install the 2.2.2 APK over 2.2 or 2.2.1. It updates in place and keeps your links and saves. Do not uninstall first.

Thanks to Velkooky on Reddit for finding and reporting this bug.

releases.name: Xenoblade DE port v0.16.1
releases.body:
## Runtime update (no visible change in this port)

This release carries a fix from the Catherine port's runtime, which both ports share.

Some games bind a block of shader constants that is shorter than what their shader actually reads. On the console the bytes just past the block are the next bytes of the game's own structure; the port was filling them with zeros. It now copies them from the game's memory up to the next 16-byte boundary and keeps zeros beyond that.

**Nothing changes in Xenoblade: its G-buffer vertex shader reads up to 368 bytes with 256 bound, and 256 is already a multiple of 16, so it keeps getting zeros — exactly as before.** Re-verified on the Flip 2 with a copy of the save: characters whole (Shulk with the Monado, the party), 30.1 fps in battle, saves untouched.

## En español

Esta versión trae un arreglo del runtime que comparte con el port de Catherine.

releases.name: Xenoblade DE port v0.16.0
releases.body:
## No more blinking objects after loading

While the game is running, each new combination of shader and render state needs a GPU pipeline. Pipelines the app has never seen are built in the background so the game doesn't freeze, and until one is ready the objects that use it are not drawn. Until now that also happened to pipelines it had already built in an earlier session. Only the first 4,000 were prepared at start-up, in the order they first appeared, so later in the game whole areas came from the background again. The result was objects and textures blinking for a few frames after loading a save or when walking into an area.

- Pipelines that the app has already built on your device are now created on the spot, in about a quarter of a millisecond each and within a small per-frame budget, so they are drawn from the first frame.
- Start-up preparation now begins with the pipelines your last session used (`pipelines_recientes.bin` in the game folder), not with the ones from the beginning of the game.
- Areas you visit for the very first time can still show an object a moment late while its pipeline is built. The second visit is clean.

releases.name: Xenoblade DE port v0.15.0
releases.body:
## Save report and update notices

Two new rows in the settings panel (swipe in from the right edge of the screen):

- **Save report** writes a folder `reports/<date>/` into your game folder: the log, a screenshot of the moment you opened the panel, the frame times of the last seconds and basic device information (model, Android version, memory). **Nothing is sent anywhere.** If something looks wrong, open an [issue](https://github.com/IamWilmar/xenoblade-recomp/issues) and attach those files (have a look first: the log contains the names of your folders).
- **Update notices** (on by default): about eight seconds after the game starts, the app asks GitHub's public API which release is the latest. It is a single request, without an account, and nothing about you or your game is sent. If there is a newer version, a banner says so and *Get vX.Y.Z* opens its page. Switch it off in the panel (or create an empty file `sin_avisos_version` in the game folder) and the app makes no network request at all.
- Because of the update notices the app now has Android's **Internet** permission. It is used for that request only.

## Installing

releases.name: v0.14.0
releases.body:
## Sharper 3D

- **The 3D image is upscaled with AMD FSR 1 before the game adds its interface.** The game draws its 3D at a dynamic resolution (for example 704×416 in handheld mode) and stretched it to its 720p window with a simple filter; on the Flip 2 that 720p image was then stretched again to the 1080p screen. Now FSR rebuilds the 3D at 720p first, and the step to 1080p sharpens instead of only stretching. The interface is untouched. The difference is largest in TV mode, where the 3D is narrowest.
- It costs about 2.8 ms of GPU per frame and turns itself off for a moment when a heavy scene would not fit in the 30 fps frame. Measured on the Flip 2 in the open field: 30 fps in handheld and TV mode.
- To get the previous image, create an empty file named `sin_fsr_escena` in the game's data folder (it takes effect while the game runs).

## Installing

Install the APK over the previous version (your settings and saves stay) or follow the [README](https://github.com/IamWilmar/xenoblade-recomp#install-and-first-run) for a first install.

## En español

releases.name: Xenoblade DE port v0.13.0
releases.body:
## Full screen, without Android's bars

- **Android's navigation bar no longer stays on top of the game.** With three-button navigation (or a visible gesture bar) the bar at the bottom of the screen covered part of the image. The app now hides the system bars while the game runs; swipe in from an edge to bring them up for a moment. Thanks to the player who reported it on a Retroid Pocket 5; it was reproduced and checked on the Flip 2.
- The settings panel opens as before: swipe left from the right half of the screen.
- To keep the bars on screen, create an empty file named `con_barras_sistema` in the game's data folder.

## Installing

Install the APK over the previous version (your settings and saves stay) or follow the [README](https://github.com/IamWilmar/xenoblade-recomp#install-and-first-run) for a first install.

## En español

releases.name: Open Bus 0.3.0
releases.body:
Open Bus 0.3.0 keeps your saves out of your game folders and lets the Commander X16 dial BBSes.

## What's new

- **Saves get their own folder.** Battery saves, save states and resume points no longer go beside your games. Each system gets its own folder, as on MiSTer: `saves/nes/Zelda.srm`, `states/nes/Zelda.state`. Saves from earlier versions are still found where they are, until the game saves again.
- **Settings → Saves:** in the desktop and Android apps, choose where saves are kept, or go back to the default; your saves move with them. See how many of each kind there are, and clear them by kind.
- **A game's saves:** a game's details list its own saves, and you can delete each one.
- **X16 games update properly.** Each X16 game runs from its own SD card. When the game's files change, for a new version say, its card is rebuilt with the new files, and anything the game saved on the card is kept. Deleting the card in the game's saves starts it fresh.

releases.name: Open Bus 0.2.2
releases.body:
Open Bus 0.2.2 fixes the macOS app and moves to SDL 2.32.

## What's new

- **macOS:** the app now opens. 0.2.1 shipped unsigned, so macOS called it damaged.
- **macOS:** the library keeps your gamepad after you quit a game, and switching pads works.
- **macOS:** 8BitDo's SN30 Pro maps by position like other pads, so its triggers fast-forward and rewind the right way round.
- **macOS:** Ctrl+Cmd+F switches fullscreen. F11 is macOS's Show Desktop shortcut. On a PC keyboard, use Ctrl+Windows key+F.
- **Everywhere:** SDL is updated from 2.26 to 2.32, with many controller fixes.
- **Linux:** SDL is built into the app, so the `.deb` and `.rpm` no longer depend on your system's SDL2.

| Windows | `.msi`, or the `-setup.exe` |
| macOS, Apple Silicon | `_aarch64.dmg` |
| macOS, Intel | `_x64.dmg` |
| Linux, Debian/Ubuntu | `.deb` |
| Linux, Fedora/openSUSE | `.rpm` |

| Android and Android TV | `.apk` |

releases.name: Open Bus 0.2.1
releases.body:
The first public release of Open Bus: old machines, emulated cycle by cycle from the 6502 up, with a game library in front of them.

**Machines:** NES and Famicom (over 70 mappers, the Disk System, the Zapper), Apple II+ and IIe, Atari 2600, Atari 7800 and Commander X16.

**Try it first in your browser:** https://obus.tuxprint.com/

No games, BIOS files or system ROMs are included. Add your own folders in Settings → Library. The [machine guide](https://github.com/bleach86/Open-Bus/blob/main/docs/machines.md) lists which system files each machine needs.

## Downloads

| System | File |
| --- | --- |
| Windows | `.msi`, or the `-setup.exe` |
| macOS, Apple Silicon | `_aarch64.dmg` |
| macOS, Intel | `_x64.dmg` |
| Linux, Debian/Ubuntu | `.deb` |
| Linux, Fedora/openSUSE | `.rpm` |
| Linux, any | `.AppImage` |
| Android and Android TV | `.apk` |

## Installing

- **Windows:** the installer isn't signed, so SmartScreen may warn. Choose *More info → Run anyway*.
- **macOS:** the app isn't notarised. The first time you open it, macOS will refuse; go to *System Settings → Privacy & Security* and choose *Open Anyway*. macOS 11 (Big Sur) or later.
